about.title: Personal Injury Help in Orange, California
about.longDescription: Orange sits near the geographic center of Orange County, and its streets carry a heavy daily load. In 2025, the most recent final crash year, the city recorded 819 injury collisions, 1,136 people injured and 6 traffic deaths. Public collision records show the highest counts along Tustin Street and Chapman Avenue, along with the southbound SR-55 and westbound SR-22. Reports tend to climb on Fridays between 5 p.m. and 7 p.m., when commuters and weekend traffic overlap around Old Towne and the Plaza. Behind each of those numbers is a person dealing with pain, missed shifts and a phone that keeps ringing with adjusters. That is where we come in. We handle personal injury cases in Orange County, and we work on a contingency basis—no fee unless there is a recovery in your case. California gives most people two years to file an injury claim, and being partly at fault does not shut the door on compensation. Whether you were rear-ended on Chapman, struck while crossing Tustin Street, or hurt somewhere else in Orange, you can get your questions answered without cost or pressure.

items.title: The clock starts sooner than you think
items.desc: California allows two years for most injury claims, but a claim against a city, county or state agency can require action in as little as six months. We can sort out which deadline applies to you.

items.title: Partial fault does not erase your claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault. If you were partly responsible, your recovery is reduced by your share, not wiped out.

items.title: No cap on pain and suffering in ordinary cases
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages in typical injury cases, so we can pursue the full human cost of what you went through, not just the bills.

items.question: How long do I have to file an injury claim in Orange, California?
items.answer: For most injury claims in California, the statute of limitations is two years from the date of the injury. If a government entity is involved, such as a city bus or a poorly maintained public sidewalk, you may have as little as six months to file a formal claim. Talking with us early helps make sure no deadline slips past.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to happen in Orange?
items.answer: Public collision records for Orange show the highest counts along Tustin Street, Chapman Avenue, southbound SR-55 and westbound SR-22. In 2025 the city recorded 819 injury collisions, and reports tend to peak on Fridays between 5 p.m. and 7 p.m. These are neutral counts from the public record, reflecting traffic volume rather than any judgment about a specific road.

items.question: What if I was partly to blame for my accident?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault. Your compensation is reduced by your percentage of responsibility, but you are not barred from recovering. Even someone found mostly at fault can still pursue the portion attributable to the other party.

items.question: Who handles my case?
